community.design-tokens.brand.imageryStyle: risograph print illustration — limited flat inks, visible grain and paper texture, slight misregistration between layers, hand-pulled feel; no photorealism, no vector slickness
community.design-tokens.brand.voice: plainspoken and unhurried; explains the method, never sells it
subjects: hands and tools working on something unfinished
schematic diagrams drawn as if printed, not rendered
small repeated marks that add up to a system
avoid: robot faces, humanoid AI mascots, glowing brains
community.design-tokens.brand.negativePrompt: no photorealism, no glossy 3D, no robot imagery, no circuit-board motifs, no stock-photo people

community.design-tokens.contrast.$comment: SKILL CONVENTION: which foreground/background pairs actually meet on screen, and at which bar. Declared because name inference reads `surface` (paper-50) and `accent` (clay-600) as screen colors, but both are print/risograph inks; and because `primary` is painted as a fill, not as type — it is held to the graphic bar, while `primary-text` carries the accent when it is set as type. Checked by `tokens contrast`.

ink-950.$description: canvas — the near-black the interface sits on

bone-100.$description: primary text on the dark canvas

slate-300.$description: secondary text and captions on the dark canvas

slate-400.$description: utility text — metadata, footnotes, page marks

amber-500.$description: the single accent as a fill or graphic mark; use amber-400 when it is type

amber-400.$description: the accent when it is set as type on the dark canvas

paper-50.$description: warm paper surface for printed / risograph contexts

clay-600.$description: second riso ink — earth red, for layered print work

slate-500.$description: mid neutral — graphic marks and print surfaces; too dark for text on the canvas
